summary: McLean's working quintet with Moncur, Hutcherson and Tony Williams replaced piano with vibes and played the East Coast including the Blue Coronet.

blocks.x: Then you got the stuff with . . .
With Grachan.
. . . with Grachan [Moncur] and Bobby [Hutcherson].
Bobby and them, yeah. That was nice. That was a nice band. We had a . . .
Tony was in that band.
Yeah. That was a good band. We rehearsed and put this music together.
Were you working?
That was a working band.
That was a working band.
Yeah, that was a working band.
Where would you be?
On the East Coast, just like you were saying. We played over in Newark. We’d play in Philadelphia. We’d play around New York, Long Island.
Did you play the Blue Coronet with this band?
With bits and pieces of it, yeah. It was not exactly that band. I played – did we play at the Coronet? Yeah, we played the Coronet. That’s right. Yeah, we played the Coronet.
When did that club become important?

I can’t remember the year, but back in the ’60s. It was just the same guys: Bobby Hutcherson, Grachan, and maybe a different drummer, different bass player. But the front line, with Bobby, Grachan, and myself, that was the concept for the harmonic structure of the music that we were playing at that particular time. Grachan wrote some the music, and I wrote some of it.
How did you come to know Grachan?

I had met Grachan early on, when I was working with the Messengers. He used to come over. We used to go to Newark, up to play. He would come to the club. He would come to the city and come to the club. But then I had never heard him play until this particular period. Then we got together and started practicing.
How did Bobby come into the mix?

Bobby had just come to New York. Somebody told me they heard this vibes player. I should check him out. So we went over to Brooklyn, had a rehearsal, invited him over. That was it. The minute I heard him, I fell in love with that whole idea, that sound, the vibes and the trombone and alto.
So you took out the piano and put in the vibes.
Put the vibes there, yeah.
